summary: @servicetitan/lazy-module ships install-time Bun-runtime dropper that executes a 728KB obfuscated payload
details: package.json declares scripts.preinstall = 'node setup.mjs'. setup.mjs is an identifier-obfuscated script that downloads the Bun runtime v1.3.13 from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases, extracts it to a temporary directory, chmods it executable, and immediately execFileSync's it against a sibling file math_init.js inside the package directory. math_init.js is a 727,680-byte single-line '// @bun @bun-cjs' blob using a shuffled string-array decoder (WV8StW rotation with a large numeric constant table) and hex-obfuscated identifiers; its contents are opaque and cannot be inspected as normal JavaScript. The package advertises itself as a ~100 LOC React Suspense wrapper, which has no need for a second language runtime or a 728KB init script. Neither setup.mjs nor math_init.js is declared in package.json's files array ('dist','src'), yet both are shipped at the tarball root and are executed by the preinstall hook on every `npm install`. Running the payload under an alternate runtime (Bun rather than Node) also evades scanners and hooks that only observe Node-resolved code paths. The @servicetitan/* scope with homepage docs.st.dev is consistent with impersonation of ServiceTitan's internal registry namespace.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
